title.zh: 卷十七 志第七 律曆中
title.en: Volume 17 Treatises 7: Rhythm and the Calendar Part Two
title.raw: 卷十七 志第七 律曆中 Volume 17 Treatises 7: Rhythm and the Calendar Part Two

sentences.zh: 律曆志中

translations.literal: Treatise on Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 昔者聖人擬宸極以運璿璣，揆天行而序景曜，分辰野，辨躔曆，敬農時，興物利，皆以系順兩儀，紀綱萬物者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the sages modeled the pole of the purple enclosure to turn the armillary sphere, measured the motion of heaven and ordered the bright luminaries, divided the asterisms and fields, distinguished the courses and calendar, revered the seasons for farming, and promoted the benefits of things; all this was to tie and harmonize the two modes and provide the guiding pattern for the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the sages took the celestial pole as their model and set the armillary sphere turning; they measured heaven’s motion and set the lights of sun, moon, and stars in their sequence; they mapped the lodges against the regions of the earth, fixed the calendar of planetary paths, honored the farmer’s seasons, and fostered the useful yield of the world—all to align the twin poles of heaven and earth and give good order to every creature under them.

sentences.zh: 然則觀象設卦，扐閏成爻，歷數之原，存乎此也。

translations.literal: Thus observing the phenomena and establishing the hexagrams, inserting intercalary months and completing the lines—the origin of calendrical reckoning—resides herein.
translations.idiomatic: From this same foundation come the observation of celestial signs, the laying out of the hexagrams, the intercalation that completes the year, and the lines of change; the root of all calendar mathematics lies here.

sentences.zh: 逮乎炎帝，分八節以始農功，軒轅紀三綱而闡書契，乃使羲和占日，常儀占月，臾區占星氣，伶倫造律呂，大撓造甲子，隸首作算數。

translations.literal: Down to the Flame Emperor, he divided the eight seasonal nodes to begin agricultural work; the Yellow Emperor recorded the three bonds and clarified writing and tallies; then he caused Xi He to observe the sun, Chang Yi to observe the moon, Yu Qu to observe the stars and vapors, Ling Lun to create the pitch-pipes, Da Nao to create the sexagenary cycle, and Li Shou to devise counting.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Flame Emperor the eight seasonal divisions were fixed to open the farming year; under the Yellow Emperor the three great norms were set down and writing took shape. Xi He was charged with the sun, Chang Yi with the moon, Yu Qu with the stars and weather signs, Ling Lun with the twelve pitch-pipes, Da Nao with the stem-and-branch cycle, and Li Shou with the art of reckoning.

sentences.zh: 容成綜斯六術，考定氣象，建五行，察發斂，起消息，正閏餘，述而著焉，謂之《調曆》。

translations.literal: Rong Cheng synthesized these six arts, examined and fixed the qi and phenomena, established the five phases, investigated expansion and contraction, initiated waxing and waning, corrected intercalary remainder, set it forth in writing, and it was called the Harmonizing Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Cheng wove these six skills into one system: he tested the seasonal qi against observation, framed the five phases, traced growth and decline, marked increase and decrease, and straightened out intercalation, then committed the whole to writing under the title Harmonizing Calendar.

sentences.zh: 洎於少昊則鳳鳥司曆，顓頊則南正司天，陶唐則分命羲和，虞舜則因循堯法。

translations.literal: Coming to Shaohao, the phoenix-birds supervised the calendar; Zhuanxu had the southern rectifier supervise heaven; lofty Yao separately commissioned Xi He; Shun of Yu followed Yao’s methods.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaohao the “phoenix officials” kept the calendar; under Zhuanxu the office of the southern rectifier watched the sky; under Yao the duties of Xi He were split among officers; Shun simply continued the institutions he had inherited from Yao.

sentences.zh: 及夏殷承運，周氏應期，正朔既殊，創法斯異。

translations.literal: When Xia and Yin received the mandate and the house of Zhou answered the appointed time, the new-year month already differed and the systems they created were thus unlike one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia and Shang took the throne in turn, and Zhou followed at its allotted hour, each dynasty chose a different first month of the year and framed its calendar in its own way.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「火出，于夏為三月，于商為四月，于周為五月。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: “When the Fire [star] emerges, in Xia it is the third month, in Shang the fourth month, in Zhou the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo commentary records: “When the Fire asterism rises heliacally, Xia reckoned it the third month of summer, Shang the fourth, and Zhou the fifth.”

sentences.zh: 」是故天子置日官，諸侯有日禦，以和萬國，以協三辰。

translations.literal: ” Therefore the Son of Heaven established sun officials; the feudal lords had sun guardians, thereby to harmonize the myriad states and to coordinate the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: ” On that account the Son of Heaven appointed officers of the sundial, and each feudal state kept its own day-keeper, so that all the realms might stay in step and sun, moon, and stars might run true to their courses.

sentences.zh: 至乎寒暑晦明之徵，陰陽生殺之數，啟閉升降之紀，消息盈虛之節，皆應躔次而無淫流，故能該浹生靈，堪輿天地。

translations.literal: As for the signs of cold and heat, dark and bright, the reckoning of yin and yang’s engendering and killing, the record of opening and closing, rising and descending, the nodes of waxing, waning, fullness, and emptiness—all correspond to the stellar positions without errant drift; therefore they can encompass living beings and pair with heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat, light and dark, the tallies by which yin and yang foster life or cut it short, the rhythm of the seasons’ opening and closing, rising and falling, waxing and waning—all of these answer to the true places of the constellations and never wander off course. That is how the calendar can embrace every living thing and stand level with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 周德既衰，史官失職，疇人分散，禨祥不理。

translations.literal: Zhou’s virtue having declined, the historiographers neglected their duties, calendar specialists scattered, and auspicious and inauspicious signs were not ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou’s moral authority faded, the court astronomers abandoned their posts, private specialists drifted apart, and no one any longer kept orderly track of omens and portents.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，頗推五勝，自以獲水德之瑞，用十月為正。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, broadly promoted the five victories, deemed itself to have obtained the auspice of the water power, and used the tenth month as the standard month.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin had conquered the empire, it pressed the doctrine of the five conquering phases, claimed the black omen of Water as its own, and took the tenth lunar month as the first month of the year.

sentences.zh: 漢氏初興，多所未暇，百有餘載，襲秦正朔。

translations.literal: When the Han house first rose, many things were not yet attended to; for more than a hundred years they inherited Qin’s standard month and new year.
translations.idiomatic: The early Han had too many crises on its hands; for well over a century it simply kept Qin’s calendar unchanged.

sentences.zh: 爰及武帝，始詔司馬遷等議造《漢曆》，乃行夏正。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu, he first ordered Sima Qian and others to deliberate on making the Han Calendar, and then the Xia standard month was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Emperor Wu did the court commission Sima Qian and his colleagues to draft a Han dynasty calendar and adopt the Xia-style first month.

sentences.zh: 其後劉歆更造夏《三統》，以說《左傳》，辯而非實，班固惑之，采以為志。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Xin remade the Xia Triple Concordance in order to expound the Zuo Commentary; it was clever but not true, Ban Gu was misled by it, and adopted it for his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin later recast the Triple Concordance calendar to force a fit with the Zuo Commentary—ingenious argument, shaky astronomy—and Ban Gu, taken in by it, built his monograph around that scheme.

sentences.zh: 逮光武中興，太僕硃浮數言曆有乖謬，于時天下初定，未能詳考。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, Grand Coachman Zhu Fu repeatedly said the calendar had errors; at that time the realm had just been pacified and a thorough investigation could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangwu restored Han, Grand Coachman Zhu Fu kept protesting that the official calendar was wrong, but the empire was only just settling and no full review could be mounted.

sentences.zh: 至永平之末，改行《四分》，七十餘年，儀式乃備。

translations.literal: By the end of the Yongping reign they changed to practice the Quarter Remainder Calendar; after more than seventy years the observational instruments and forms were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of Yongping the court switched to the Quarter Remainder system; only after seventy-odd years did instruments and ritual procedure catch up.

sentences.zh: 及光和中，乃命劉洪、蔡邕共修律曆，其後司馬彪因之，以繼班史。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe period they ordered Liu Hong and Cai Yong jointly to revise the pitch-pipes and calendar; afterward Sima Biao followed this to continue Ban Gu’s history.
translations.idiomatic: During Guanghe, Liu Hong and Cai Yong were told to overhaul harmonics and calendrics together; Sima Biao later took their work as the basis for the treatise that follows Ban Gu’s Han shu.

sentences.zh: 今采魏文黃初已後言歷數行事者，以續司馬彪雲。

translations.literal: Now I gather those who, from Wei Wendi’s Huangchu reign onward, spoke of calendrical reckoning and practice, in order to continue Sima Biao.
translations.idiomatic: What follows collects, from Wei Wendi’s Huangchu era on, every substantive discussion of calendar theory and practice, extending the thread that Sima Biao began.

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝時，會稽東部尉劉洪，考史官自古迄今曆注，原其進退之行，察其出入之驗，視其往來，度其終始，始悟《四分》於天疏闊，皆斗分太多故也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling of Han, Liu Hong, eastern commandery captain of Kuaiji, examined the calendar annotations of the historiographers from antiquity to the present, traced the advance and retreat of their motions, investigated the verification of their emergence and entry, observed their comings and goings, and measured their ends and beginnings; then he first realized the Quarter Remainder was loose relative to heaven, all because the dipper fraction was too large.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling, Liu Hong of Kuaiji, while serving as eastern commandery captain, combed the court’s calendar notes from the oldest records down to his own day, tracking how the bodies sped up or slowed, checking predicted risings and settings against fact, and mapping their whole cycle—until he saw that the Quarter Remainder calendar simply did not hug the sky closely enough, and that the fault lay in making the “dipper fraction” too generous.

sentences.zh: 更以五百八十九為紀法，百四十五為斗分，作《乾象法》，冬至日日在鬥二十二度，以術追日、月、五星之行，推而上則合于古，引而下則應於今。

translations.literal: He further took 589 as the era divisor and 145 as the dipper fraction, and made the Qianxiang Method; on the winter solstice the sun was at 22 degrees in Dipper; using the technique to pursue the motions of sun, moon, and five planets, pushing upward it agreed with antiquity, drawing downward it responded to the present.
translations.idiomatic: He set the cycle divisor at 589 and the dipper fraction at 145, producing what is called the Qianxiang system: at winter solstice the sun stood at 22° within the Dipper lodge. His algorithms for the sun, moon, and five planets match ancient records when projected backward and track the sky we see today when carried forward.

sentences.zh: 其為之也，依《易》立數，遁行相號，潛處相求，名為《乾象曆》。

translations.literal: In making it, he relied on the Changes to establish numbers, with hidden motion mutually designating, concealed positions mutually seeking; it was named the Qianxiang Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The structure rests on numerology drawn from the Book of Changes: hidden motions call to one another across the sky, and latent positions are solved for one another—the whole was published as the Qianxiang calendar.

sentences.zh: 又創制日行遲速，兼考月行，陰陽交錯于黃道表裏，日行黃道，於赤道宿度復有進退。

translations.literal: He also first devised the sun’s slowing and quickening, and concurrently examined the moon’s motion; yin and yang interweave inside and outside the ecliptic; the sun moves along the ecliptic, and relative to the equatorial lodge degrees there is again advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to model the sun’s unequal motion and at the same time to refine the moon’s path, tracing how lunar and solar motion weave above and below the ecliptic while the sun itself slides along the ecliptic and still gains or loses ground against the equatorial longitudes.

sentences.zh: 方於前法，轉為精密矣。

translations.literal: Compared with the previous methods, it became more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the older procedures, this was a marked gain in precision.

sentences.zh: 獻帝建安元年，鄭玄受其法，以為窮幽極微，又加注釋焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian’an of Emperor Xian, Zheng Xuan received his method, deemed it to exhaust the subtle and reach the minute, and further added commentary and glosses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jian’an year the great scholar Zheng Xuan studied Liu Hong’s system, pronounced it the last word in subtlety, and furnished it with a full commentary.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初中，太史令高堂隆復詳議歷數，更有改革。

translations.literal: In Wei Wendi’s Huangchu period, the Grand Astrologer Gao Tanglong again exhaustively debated calendrical reckoning, and there was further reform.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei’s Huangchu reign, Grand Astrologer Gao Tanglong reopened the debate on the calendar and further changes were proposed.

sentences.zh: 太史丞韓翊以為《乾象》減斗分太過，後當先天，造《黃初曆》，以四千八百八十三為紀法，千二百五為斗分。

translations.literal: Assistant Grand Astrologer Han Yi thought the Qianxiang had reduced the dipper fraction too much and later would anticipate heaven; he created the Huangchu Calendar, taking 4883 as the era divisor and 1250 as the dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy astrologer Han Yi argued that Qianxiang had pared the dipper fraction too sharply and would eventually run ahead of the sky; he therefore drafted the Huangchu calendar, with a cycle divisor of 4883 and a dipper fraction of 1250.

sentences.zh: 其後尚書令陳群奏，以為：「歷數難明，前代通儒多共紛爭。

translations.literal: Afterward Minister of Works Chen Qun memorialized, saying: “Calendrical reckoning is hard to clarify; learned scholars of former ages often disputed it together.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Qun then submitted a memorial: “Calendar theory is notoriously opaque, and fine scholars of past dynasties rarely agreed.”

sentences.zh: 《黃初》之元以《四分曆》久遠疏闊，大魏受命，宜改曆明時，韓翊首建，猶鞏不審，故以《乾象》互相參校。

translations.literal: The origin of the Huangchu [calendar took as its ground that] the Quarter Remainder Calendar had long been loose; Great Wei received the mandate and ought to reform the calendar to clarify the seasons; Han Yi first proposed it, but still obstinately did not examine carefully, therefore they mutually cross-checked with the Qianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangchu reform began from the premise that the old Quarter Remainder had grown hopelessly slack; now that Wei held the mandate, the seasons needed a new calendar. Han Yi opened the discussion, yet his work still lacked rigorous vetting, so the Qianxiang system was brought in for a side-by-side test.”

sentences.zh: 其所校日月行度，弦望朔晦，曆三年，更相是非，無時而決。

translations.literal: What they cross-checked—the motions of sun and moon, quarters, full moons, new moons, and dark moons—for three years they alternately judged right and wrong, and there was no time when it was decided.
translations.idiomatic: They compared solar and lunar positions, first and last quarters, full and new moons, for three years, trading contradictory verdicts without ever reaching a settlement.”

sentences.zh: 案三公議皆綜盡典理，殊塗同歸，欲使效之璿璣，各盡其法，一年之間，得失足定。

translations.literal: According to the three dukes’ deliberations, all comprehensively exhaust canonical principle; different paths have the same return; they wish to have them tested on the armillary sphere, each exhausting its method; within one year gain and loss would be sufficient to determine.
translations.idiomatic: The three high ministers replied that every proposal drew on solid classical principle and aimed at the same end by different routes; the thing to do was to run each system on the armillary instrument for a full year—then success and failure would show plainly.”

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: ” The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 太史令許芝云：「劉洪月行術用以來且四十餘年，以復覺失一辰有奇。」

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Xu Zhi said: “Liu Hong’s lunar motion method has been in use approaching more than forty years, and again it is perceived to miss by more than one chen.”
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Xu Zhi observed: “We have relied on Liu Hong’s lunar theory for the better part of forty years, and it is now drifting off by well over one-twelfth of a day.”

sentences.zh: 孫飲議：「史遷造《太初》，其後劉歆以為疏，復為《三統》。

translations.literal: Sun Yin deliberated: “Sima Qian made the Taichu; afterward Liu Xin thought it loose and again made the Triple Concordance.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yin argued: “Sima Qian framed the Taichu calendar; Liu Xin later judged it coarse and replaced it with the Triple Concordance.”

sentences.zh: 章和中，改為《四分》，以儀天度，考合符應，時有差跌，日蝕覺過半日。

translations.literal: In the Zhanghe period it was changed to the Quarter Remainder, using instruments to measure celestial degrees and examine compliance with signs; at times there were slips, and solar eclipses were perceived to miss by more than half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhanghe the court adopted the Quarter Remainder and checked it with instruments against heaven; slips still occurred—solar eclipses were sometimes half a day out.”

sentences.zh: 至熹平中，劉洪改為《乾象》，推天七曜之符，與天地合其敘。」

translations.literal: By the Xiping period Liu Hong changed it to the Qianxiang, pushing the signs of the seven luminaries of heaven, and with heaven and earth it matched their sequence.”
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping years Liu Hong introduced Qianxiang, which lines up the seven lights with celestial signs and keeps heaven and earth in the same story.”

sentences.zh: 董巴議云：「聖人跡太陽于晷景，效太陰於弦望，明五星於見伏，正是非於晦朔。

translations.literal: Dong Ba deliberated, saying: “The sages trace the great yang in gnomon shadow, model the great yin on quarters and full moons, clarify the five planets in visibility and concealment, and correct right and wrong on dark and new moons.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ba said: “The sages ground the sun in the noon shadow, tested the moon against quarters and full moons, fixed the five planets by their appearances and disappearances, and settled true from false at new and full moon.”

sentences.zh: 弦望伏見者，歷數之綱紀，檢驗之明者也。」

translations.literal: Quarters, full moons, concealment, and visibility are the guiding cords of calendrical reckoning, and the clarity of verification.”
translations.idiomatic: First quarter, full moon, first visibility, and last sight—these are the backbone of any calendar and the cleanest tests we have.”

sentences.zh: 徐嶽議：「劉洪以曆後天，潛精內思二十餘載，參校漢家《太初》、《三統》、《四分》曆術，課弦望于兩儀郭間。

translations.literal: Xu Yue deliberated: “Liu Hong, because the calendar lagged heaven, inwardly pondered deeply for more than twenty years, cross-checked the Han house’s Taichu, Triple Concordance, and Quarter Remainder calendrical arts, and tested quarters and full moons between the two instrument rings.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yue replied: “Seeing that the official calendar fell behind the sky, Liu Hong brooded for twenty years over the Taichu, Triple Concordance, and Quarter Remainder systems, checking quarter- and full-moon predictions against the paired armillary circles.”

sentences.zh: 而月行九歲一終，謂之九道；

translations.literal: And the moon’s motion completes one cycle in nine years; it is called the nine paths;
translations.idiomatic: He showed that the moon completes a nine-year cycle of paths—the so-called nine roads;

sentences.zh: 九章，百七十一歲，九道小終；

translations.literal: nine chapters, 171 years, the nine paths’ small completion;
translations.idiomatic: nine rounds make 171 years, the minor closure of the nine paths;

sentences.zh: 九九八十一章，五百六十七分而九終，進退牛前四度五分。

translations.literal: nine times nine eighty-one chapters, 567 parts and the nine cycles end, advancing and retreating before the Ox by four and five-fifths degrees.
translations.idiomatic: nine times nine, or eighty-one chapters, span 567 fractional parts to finish the great ninefold cycle, with residual motion of four and five-fifths degrees short of the Ox lodge.”

sentences.zh: 學者務追合《四分》，但減一道六十三分，分不下通，是以疏闊，皆由斗分多故也。

translations.literal: Scholars strove to chase agreement with the Quarter Remainder, only reducing one path sixty-three parts; the parts did not communicate downward; therefore it was loose, all because the dipper fraction was too large.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars tried to patch the Quarter Remainder by shaving one path sixty-three parts, but the fractions would not reconcile downward, so the fit stayed loose—the dipper fraction was simply too big.”

sentences.zh: 課弦望當以昏明度月所在，則知加時先後之意，不宜用兩儀郭間。

translations.literal: Testing quarters and full moons ought to use dusk and dawn to measure where the moon is, then one knows the meaning of the added hour’s before and after; one should not use the space between the two instrument rings.
translations.idiomatic: Quarter- and full-moon tests should fix the moon’s place at dusk and dawn so you can see whether the predicted hour runs early or late; the gap between the two armillary rings is the wrong place to measure.”

sentences.zh: 洪加《太初》元十二紀，減十斗下分，元起己丑，又為月行遲疾交會及黃道去極度、五星術，理實粹密，信可長行。

translations.literal: Hong added twelve eras to the Taichu origin, reduced ten dipper lower parts, the origin rose at jichou, and also made for lunar motion slow and fast, conjunction, and ecliptic departure from the pole and five-planet methods; the principle is truly pure and dense, and truly can be practiced long.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong extended the Taichu epoch by twelve cycles, trimmed the lower dipper fraction by ten parts, began the count at the jichou year, and added models for the moon’s speed, syzygies, ecliptic latitude, and the five planets—the theory is tight and durable enough to serve for generations.”

sentences.zh: 今韓翊所造，皆用洪法，小益鬥下分，所錯無幾。

translations.literal: Now what Han Yi has created all uses Hong’s method, slightly increasing the dipper lower part; the error is not much.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi’s calendar is Liu Hong’s with a slightly larger lower dipper fraction—the deviation is tiny.”

sentences.zh: 翊所增減，致亦留思，然十術新立，猶未就悉，至於日蝕，有不盡效。

translations.literal: What Yi increased and decreased, the result also shows thoughtful care, yet the ten arts are newly established and still not fully complete; as for solar eclipses, there are places where the effect is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: His adjustments show care, but the ten new procedures are not fully debugged; on solar eclipses they still misfire sometimes.”

sentences.zh: 效曆之要，要在日蝕。

translations.literal: The essential point of testing a calendar, the essential lies in solar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: If you want to prove a calendar, solar eclipses are the decisive test.”

sentences.zh: 熹平之際，時洪為郎，欲改《四分》，先上驗日蝕：日蝕在晏，加時在辰，蝕從下上，三分侵二。

translations.literal: At the time of Xiping, at that time Hong was a gentleman, wishing to reform the Quarter Remainder, he first submitted verification of a solar eclipse: the solar eclipse was at late in the day, the added hour was in chen, the eclipse was from below upward, two-thirds of three parts encroached.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiping, Liu Hong—then a court gentleman—petitioned to replace the Quarter Remainder and led with a solar-eclipse check: the eclipse fell late in the day, the true hour landed in the fifth double-hour, shadow crept upward from the lower limb, and two-thirds of the disk was eaten.”

sentences.zh: 事禦之後如洪言，海內識真，莫不聞見，劉歆以來，未有洪比。

translations.literal: After the matter was presented to the throne it was as Hong said; within the seas those who knew the true all heard and saw; since Liu Xin there has been none comparable to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When the event was over, observation matched Hong’s prediction; everyone who understood astronomy saw it, and since Liu Xin’s day no one has rivaled him.”

sentences.zh: 夫以黃初二年六月二十九日戊辰加時未日蝕，《乾象術》加時申半強，於消息就加未，《黃初》以為加辛強，《乾象》後天一辰半強為近，《黃初》二辰半為遠，消息與天近。

translations.idiomatic: Li En of the Langzhong bureau testified: “When we stacked our figures against the official sky-longitudes, the full moons of the seventh month (year two) and the eleventh month (year three) both failed to line up with the solar count; the lunar eclipse’s predicted moment ran six and a half double-hours behind the heavens—far more than a three-degree slip—so we are dealing with a solid half-day lag.”

translations.idiomatic: Dong Ba continued: “Legend says Fuxi first drew the eight trigrams in three lines each, emblematizing the twenty-four seasonal nodes.”

translations.idiomatic: Across eleven royal houses and some five thousand counted years, seven distinct calendrical systems appeared.

sentences.zh: 顓頊以今之孟春正月為元，其時正月朔旦立春，五星會于廟，營室也，冰凍始泮，蟄蟲始發，雞始三號，天曰作時，地曰作昌，人曰作樂，鳥獸萬物莫不應和，故顓頊聖人為曆宗也。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu took the present first month of early spring as origin; at that time the first month’s new-moon dawn was Beginning of Spring; the five planets met at the temple—it was Encampment; ice and freeze first melted, hibernating insects first stirred, the fowl first crowed thrice; heaven was called making the seasons, earth was called making prosperity, man was called making joy; birds, beasts, and the myriad things none did not respond in harmony; therefore Zhuanxu the sage was the patriarch of calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu fixed his era to what we now call the first month of early spring: new moon and dawn coincided with Beginning of Spring, the five planets gathered over the ritual hall in the Encampment lodge, ice broke, dormant creatures stirred, and cocks crowed thrice—heaven was said to “open the seasons,” earth to “flourish,” and mankind to “take joy,” while every bird and beast fell into step. That is why Zhuanxu is remembered as the founding sage of calendrics.”

sentences.zh: 湯作《殷曆》弗復以正月朔旦立春為節也，更以十一月朔旦冬至為元首，下至周魯及漢，皆從其節，據正四時。

translations.literal: Tang made the Yin Calendar and no longer took the first month’s new-moon dawn Beginning of Spring as the node; he changed to take the eleventh month’s new-moon dawn winter solstice as the head origin; down to Zhou, Lu, and Han, all followed this node, relying on it to rectify the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang’s Yin calendar abandoned the old rule that new year begin with new moon and Beginning of Spring; instead it enthroned the eleventh month’s new moon at winter solstice as the year’s pivot. Zhou, Lu, and Han all kept that hinge and used it to true the four seasons.”

sentences.zh: 夏為得天，以承堯舜，從顓頊故也。

translations.literal: Xia obtained heaven; thereby inheriting Yao and Shun, following Zhuanxu’s reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar was said to “accord with heaven” because it continued the practice Yao and Shun had taken over from Zhuanxu.”

sentences.zh: 楊偉請：「六十日中疏密可知，不待十年。

sentences.zh: 至明帝景初元年，尚書郎楊偉造《景初曆》。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ming’s first year of Jingchu, Director of the Ministry Yang Wei made the Jingchu Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jingchu year of Emperor Ming, Yang Wei of the secretariat produced the Jingchu calendar.

sentences.zh: 表上，帝遂改正朔，施行偉曆，以建丑之月為正，改其年三月為孟夏，其孟、仲、季月雖與夏正不同，至於郊祀蒐狩，班宣時令，皆以建寅為正。

translations.literal: He presented a memorial upward; the emperor thereupon changed the standard month and new year, implemented Wei’s calendar, took the month established in chou as correct, changed that year’s third month to early summer; although its first, second, and third months of the season differed from the Xia standard, as for suburban sacrifice, hunt, promulgating and proclaiming seasonal orders, all took the month established in yin as correct.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his memorial, reset the civil year, and adopted Yang Wei’s calendar: the chou month became month one, and the old third month was relabeled early summer. Seasonal names no longer matched the Xia calendar, yet for suburban rites, royal hunts, and publishing the seasonal edicts, the yin month still counted as the true pivot of the year.

sentences.zh: 三年正月帝崩，復用夏正。

translations.literal: Third year first month the emperor died; they again used the Xia standard month.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died in the first month of the third year, the court reverted to the Xia-style first month.

sentences.zh: 其劉氏在蜀，仍漢《四分曆》。

translations.literal: As for the Liu clan in Shu, they continued the Han Quarter Remainder Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu house in Shu simply kept Han’s Quarter Remainder calendar.

sentences.zh: 吳中書令闞澤受劉洪《乾象法》于東萊徐嶽，又加解注。

translations.literal: Wu’s Director of the Secretariat Kan Ze received Liu Hong’s Qianxiang Method from Xu Yue of Donglai, and further added exegesis and commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze, Wu’s chief secretary, studied Liu Hong’s Qianxiang method under Xu Yue of Donglai and supplied his own commentary.

sentences.zh: 中常待王蕃以洪術精妙，用推渾天之理，以制儀象及論，故孫氏用《乾象曆》，至吳亡。

translations.literal: Palace Regular Attendant Wang Fan, because Hong’s method was subtle and fine, used it to infer the principle of the spherical heaven, thereby to regulate instruments, armillary models, and treatises; therefore the Sun house used the Qianxiang Calendar, until Wu fell.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Wang Fan, impressed by the finesse of Hong’s mathematics, applied it to spherical-heaven theory and built instruments and treatises on that basis, so the Sun regime employed the Qianxiang calendar until Wu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，泰始元年，因魏之《景初曆》，改名《泰始曆》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, first year of Taishi, following Wei’s Jingchu Calendar, he changed the name to Taishi Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu’s accession year Taishi simply inherited Wei’s Jingchu system and rechristened it the Taishi calendar.

sentences.zh: 楊偉推五星尤疏闊，故元帝渡江左以後，更以《乾象》五星法代偉曆。

translations.literal: Yang Wei’s pushing of the five planets was especially loose; therefore after Emperor Yuan crossed to the left of the river, they replaced Wei’s calendar with the Qianxiang five-planet method.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei’s planetary tables were particularly slack, so once Emperor Yuan moved the court south of the Yangzi, the Qianxiang planetary rules supplanted Wei’s calendar.

sentences.zh: 自黃初已後，改作曆術，皆斟酌《乾象》所減斗分、朔餘、月行陰陽遲疾，以求折衷。

translations.literal: From Huangchu onward, revised calendrical arts all weighed the Qianxiang’s reduced dipper fraction, new-moon remainder, and lunar motion’s yin-yang slow and fast, seeking a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: Every calendar reform after Huangchu tinkered with Liu Hong’s trimmed dipper fraction, lunation remainder, and model of the moon’s speeding and slowing in order to strike a middle path.

sentences.zh: 洪術為後代推步之師表，故先列之雲。

translations.literal: Hong’s method is the model for later generations’ ephemeris computation; therefore it is first set forth thus.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Hong’s work became the classroom standard for later astronomers, it is presented here first.

sentences.zh: 乾象曆

translations.literal: Qianxiang Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianxiang Calendar.

sentences.zh: 上元己丑以來，至建安十一年丙戌，歲積七千三百七十八年。

translations.literal: From high origin jichou down to Jian’an eleventh year bingxu, year accumulation 7378.
translations.idiomatic: From the epoch year jichou to bingxu, the eleventh year of Jian’an, the accumulated year count is 7378.

sentences.zh: 乾法，千一百七十八。

translations.literal: Qian divisor, 1178.
translations.idiomatic: Qian divisor: 1178.

sentences.zh: 會通，七千一百七十一。

translations.literal: Hui tong, 7171.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction cycle constant: 7171.

sentences.zh: 紀法，五百八十九。

translations.literal: Era divisor, 589.
translations.idiomatic: Era divisor: 589.

sentences.zh: 周天，二十一萬五千一百三十。

translations.literal: Full heaven [circumference parts], 215130.
translations.idiomatic: Full celestial circle, in parts: 215,130.

sentences.zh: 通法，四萬三千二十六。

translations.literal: Tong divisor, 43026.
translations.idiomatic: Common divisor: 43,026.

sentences.zh: 通數，三十一。

translations.literal: Tong number, 31.
translations.idiomatic: Common factor: 31.

sentences.zh: 日法，千四百五十七。

translations.literal: Day divisor, 1457.
translations.idiomatic: Day denominator: 1457.

sentences.zh: 歲中，十二。

translations.literal: Months in a year, 12.
translations.idiomatic: Months per solar year: 12.

sentences.zh: 餘數，三千九十。

translations.literal: Remainder number, 3090.
translations.idiomatic: Solar remainder constant: 3090.

sentences.zh: 章歲，十九。

translations.literal: Metonic cycle years, 19.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen-year metonic cycle.

sentences.zh: 沒法，百三。

translations.literal: Extinction divisor, 103.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary extinction divisor: 103.

sentences.zh: 章閏，七。

translations.literal: Metonic intercalations, 7.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary months per metonic cycle: 7.

sentences.zh: 會數，四十七。

translations.literal: Conjunction number, 47.
translations.idiomatic: Lunation factor: 47.

sentences.zh: 會歲，八百九十三。

translations.literal: Conjunction years, 893.
translations.idiomatic: Great conjunction period: 893 years.

sentences.zh: 章月，二百三十五。

translations.literal: Metonic months, 235.
translations.idiomatic: Months in a metonic cycle: 235.

sentences.zh: 會率，千八百八十二。

translations.literal: Conjunction rate, 1882.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction modulus: 1882.

sentences.zh: 朔望合數，九百四十一。

translations.literal: New and full moon combined number, 941.
translations.idiomatic: New- and full-moon combination number: 941.

sentences.zh: 會月，萬一千四十五。

translations.literal: Conjunction months, 11045.
translations.idiomatic: Months in the great conjunction cycle: 11,045.

sentences.zh: 紀月，七千二百八十五。

translations.literal: Era months, 7285.
translations.idiomatic: Months per era unit: 7285.

sentences.zh: 元月，一萬四千五百七十。

translations.literal: Origin months, 14570.
translations.idiomatic: Origin-cycle month count: 14,570.

sentences.zh: 月周，七千八百七十四。

translations.literal: Lunar circuit, 7874.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar revolution constant: 7874.

sentences.zh: 小周，二百五十四。

translations.literal: Small cycle, 254.
translations.idiomatic: Minor lunar cycle: 254.

sentences.zh: 推入紀

translations.literal: Procedure: entering the era count.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: find the position within the era.

sentences.zh: 置上元盡所求年，以乾法除之，不滿乾法，以紀法除之，余不滿紀法者，入內紀甲子年也。

translations.literal: Set high origin exhausted to the sought year, divide by the Qian divisor; what does not fill the Qian divisor, divide by the era divisor; the remainder that does not fill the era divisor enters inner era, a jiazi year.
translations.idiomatic: Take the years from the high origin to the target year, divide by the Qian divisor; with the remainder divide by the era divisor; any remainder still smaller than the era divisor lands you in the inner era beginning with jiazi.

sentences.zh: 滿法去之，入外紀甲午年也。

translations.literal: Filling the divisor, remove it; enter outer era jiawu year.
translations.idiomatic: If the remainder fills the divisor, strip it out and you are in the outer era that starts with jiawu.

sentences.zh: 置入紀年，外所求，以章月乘之，章歲而一，所得為定積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Set entering-era years, outside the sought, multiply by metonic months, divide by metonic years; what is obtained is fixed accumulated months; what is not exhausted is intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the years since era entry by 235 and divide by 19; the quotient is the accumulated month count and the remainder is the intercalary residue.

sentences.zh: 閏餘十二以上，歲有閏。

translations.literal: Intercalary remainder twelve and above, the year has an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary remainder reaches twelve or more, insert a leap month that year.

sentences.zh: 以通法乘定積月，為假積日，滿日法為定積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply fixed accumulated months by the tong divisor, obtaining provisional accumulated days; what fills the day divisor is fixed accumulated days; what is not exhausted is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the accumulated months by the tong divisor to get provisional day-count; divide by the day denominator for whole days, leaving the fractional day as the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日為大餘，命以所入紀，算外，所求年天正十一月朔日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixty-day cycles from accumulated days for large remainder; assign according to the entered era, outside the count; this is the sought year’s celestial standard eleventh month new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out multiples of sixty from the day total for the stem-branch remainder; count it off within the current era cycle—what lies beyond the count is new moon of the eleventh civil month of the standard year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘七百七十三，小餘滿日法從大餘。

translations.literal: Seek next month: add large remainder 29, small remainder 773; small remainder filling day divisor carries to large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 to the large remainder and 773 to the small; whenever the small part overflows the day denominator, carry into the large remainder.

sentences.zh: 小餘六百八十四已上，其月大。

translations.literal: Small remainder 684 and above, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: A small remainder of 684 or more marks a long month.

sentences.zh: 推冬至

translations.literal: Procedure: winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 置入紀年，外所求，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Set entering-era years, outside the sought, multiply by the remainder number; what fills the era divisor is large remainder; what is not exhausted is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the years since era entry by the solar remainder constant; divide by the era divisor—the quotient is the large remainder, the residue the small.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去之，命以紀，算外，天正冬至日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixty-day cycles from it, assign by era, outside the count; this is celestial standard winter solstice day.
translations.idiomatic: Drop sixties, assign within the era count, and the remainder beyond the tally is winter solstice of the standard year.

sentences.zh: 求二十四氣

translations.literal: Procedure: the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: the twenty-four solar terms.

sentences.zh: 置冬至小餘，加大餘十五，小餘五百一十五，滿二千三百五十六從大餘，命如法。

translations.literal: Set winter solstice small remainder, add large remainder 15, small remainder 515; what fills 2356 carries to large remainder; assign by the method.
translations.idiomatic: From the winter solstice fractions add 15 to the large part and 515 to the small; carry 2356 from the small into the large; continue the count by the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 推閏月

translations.literal: Procedure: intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 以閏餘減章歲，餘以歲中乘之，滿章閏為一月。

translations.literal: Subtract intercalary remainder from metonic years; multiply the remainder by months in a year; what fills metonic intercalations is one month.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the intercalary residue from 19, multiply the difference by 12, and divide by 7—the quotient tells how many leap months to insert.

sentences.zh: 不盡，半法己上亦一，有進退，以無中月。

translations.literal: Not exhausted, half divisor and above also one; there is advance and retreat, by the month without mid-qi.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a leftover half the divisor or more, add another month; adjust forward or backward so the leap month lacks a mid-season qi.

sentences.zh: 推弦望

translations.literal: Procedure: quarters and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: first quarter, full moon, last quarter.

sentences.zh: 加大餘七，小餘五百五十七半，小餘如日法從大餘，餘命如前，得上弦。

translations.literal: Add large remainder 7, small remainder 557 and a half; small remainder like day divisor carries to large remainder; assign remainder as before, obtaining first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Add 7 to the large remainder and 557½ to the small; carry overflows of the day denominator; count off as before to reach first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加得望，又加得下弦，又加得後月朔。

translations.literal: Again add to obtain full moon; again add to obtain last quarter; again add to obtain next month’s new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the step for full moon, again for last quarter, and again for the next new moon.

sentences.zh: 其弦望定小餘四百一以下，以百刻乘之，滿日法得一刻，不盡什之，求分，以課所近節氣夜漏未盡，以算上為日。

translations.literal: If their quarter and full moon fixed small remainder is 401 and below, multiply by hundred ke; what fills day divisor obtains one ke; what is not exhausted, divide by ten, seeking parts, to test the nearest qi’s night clepsydra not yet exhausted; by the count above as day.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional part of a quarter or full moon is 401 or less, multiply by 100 ke, divide by the day denominator for whole ke, subdivide the remainder by ten for finer parts, and compare with the night run of the neighboring qi—if the water-clock has not run out, count it to the previous day.

sentences.zh: 置入紀年，外所求，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為積沒，有餘加盡積為一。

translations.literal: Set entering-era years, outside the sought, multiply by remainder number; what fills era divisor is accumulated extinction; if there is remainder, add exhausting accumulated as one.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply years since era entry by the solar remainder; divide by the era divisor for accumulated extinction days; if anything remains, add a full cycle.

sentences.zh: 以會通乘之，滿沒法為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply by hui tong; what fills extinction divisor is large remainder; what is not exhausted is small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the conjunction constant; divide by 103 for the large remainder, the residue is the small.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以紀，算外，冬至後沒日。

translations.literal: Large remainder assign by era, outside the count, day after winter solstice of extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Count the large remainder within the era; the tally after it marks the first “extinction” day following winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加大餘六十九，小餘六十四，滿其法從大餘，無分為滅。

translations.literal: Seek next extinction: add large remainder 69, small remainder 64; what fills its divisor carries to large remainder; no fraction means extinction.
translations.idiomatic: For the next extinction add 69 and 64; carry when full; zero fraction signals complete extinction.

sentences.zh: 推日度

translations.literal: Procedure: solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: solar longitude.

sentences.zh: 以紀法乘積日，滿周天去之，余以紀法除之，所得為度。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated days by era divisor; remove what fills full heaven; remainder divide by era divisor; what is obtained is degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply elapsed days by 589, discard multiples of the celestial circumference, divide the remainder by 589—the quotient is degrees of motion.

sentences.zh: 命度以牛前五度起，宿次除之，不滿宿，即天正朔夜半日所在。

translations.literal: Assign degrees starting from five degrees before Ox; remove by lodge order; what does not fill a lodge is where the sun is at celestial standard new-moon midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Begin counting from five degrees before the Ox lodge, step through successive mansions, and the fractional lodge at standard new-moon midnight is the sun’s place.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一度，經鬥除分；

translations.literal: Seek next day: add one degree, passing Dipper remove fraction;
translations.idiomatic: For the next day add one degree; when you cross through Dipper, drop the fractional part;

sentences.zh: 分少，損一度為紀法，加焉。

translations.literal: fraction small, subtract one degree for era divisor, add thereto.
translations.idiomatic: if the fraction is too small, borrow one degree as 589 parts and add.

sentences.zh: 推月度

translations.literal: Procedure: lunar degree.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: lunar longitude.

sentences.zh: 以月周乘積日，滿周天去之，余滿紀法為度，不盡為分，命如上，則天正朔夜半月所在度。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated days by lunar circuit; remove what fills full heaven; remainder filling era divisor is degrees, not exhausted is parts; assign as above; then celestial standard new-moon midnight moon’s place in degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply days by the lunar circuit constant, reduce modulo the sky circle, divide by 589 for whole degrees with remainder as minutes, and assign mansions as for the sun—this is the moon’s longitude at standard new-moon midnight.

sentences.zh: 求次月，小月加度二十二，分二百五十八。

translations.literal: Seek next month, short month add degrees 22, parts 258.
translations.idiomatic: After a short month add 22°258′ to the moon’s position.

sentences.zh: 大月又加一日，度十三，分二百一十七，滿法得一度。

translations.literal: Long month again add one day, degrees 13, parts 217; filling divisor obtains one degree.
translations.idiomatic: After a long month add another day’s worth—13°217′—and carry 589 parts to one degree.

sentences.zh: 其冬下旬，月在張、心署之。

translations.literal: Its winter latter ten-day period, moon in Zhang, Heart mark it.
translations.idiomatic: In the last third of winter, note the moon against Zhang and Heart.

sentences.zh: 推合朔度

translations.literal: Procedure: conjunction degree.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: syzygy longitude.

sentences.zh: 以章歲乘朔小餘，滿會數為大分；

translations.literal: Multiply new-moon small remainder by metonic years; what fills conjunction number is large fraction;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the lunation fraction by 19; divide by 47 for the major fraction;

sentences.zh: 不盡，小分。

translations.literal: not exhausted, small fraction.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder is the minor fraction.

sentences.zh: 以大分從朔夜半日分，滿紀法從度，命如前，天正合朔日月所共會也。

translations.literal: Take large fraction following new-moon midnight sun fraction; what fills era divisor carries to degrees; assign as before; celestial standard conjunction is where sun and moon jointly meet.
translations.idiomatic: Add the major fraction to the sun’s midnight position on new moon, carry 589 into degrees, and count mansions as before—this locates the true conjunction of sun and moon for the standard month.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加度二十九，大分三百一十二，小分滿會數從大分，大分滿紀法後度，經鬥除大分。

translations.literal: Seek next month, add degrees 29, large fraction 312; small fraction filling conjunction number carries to large fraction; large fraction filling era divisor goes to later degree; passing Dipper remove large fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For the next syzygy add 29°312′ plus fractional carries through 47 and 589, and strip the large fraction when crossing Dipper.

sentences.zh: 求弦望日所在度，加合朔度七，分二百二十五，小分十七半，大小分及度命如前，則上弦日所在度。

translations.literal: Seek quarter and full moon sun’s place in degrees: add to conjunction degrees 7, parts 225, small parts 17 and a half; large and small parts and degrees assign as before; then first quarter sun’s place in degrees.
translations.idiomatic: To place the sun at quarter or full phase, add 7°225′17½″ to the conjunction longitude, carrying and assigning as before to obtain first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加得望、下弦、後月合。

translations.literal: Again add to obtain full moon, last quarter, next month conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the increment for full moon, last quarter, and the next conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求弦望月行所在度，加合朔度九十八，大分四百八，小分四十一，大小分及度命如前合朔，則上弦月所在。

translations.literal: Seek quarter and full moon moon motion’s place in degrees: add to conjunction degrees 98, large fraction 408, small fraction 41; large and small parts and degrees assign as before conjunction; then first quarter moon’s place.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon at quarters and full, add 98°408′41″ to the conjunction longitude, using the same carrying rules, to fix first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加得望、下弦、後月合。

translations.literal: Again add to obtain full moon, last quarter, next month conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Iterate again for full moon, last quarter, and following new moon.

sentences.zh: 求日月昏明度，日以紀法，月以月周，乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一為明分。

translations.literal: Seek sun and moon dusk and dawn degrees: sun by era divisor, moon by lunar circuit, multiply the nearest qi’s night clepsydra; divide by two hundred for bright fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For dawn and dusk positions, multiply the night run of the neighboring qi by 589 for the sun or by the lunar circuit for the moon, then divide by 200 to get the bright fraction.

sentences.zh: 日以減紀法，月以減月周，餘為昏分。

translations.literal: Sun subtract from era divisor, moon subtract from lunar circuit; remainder is dusk fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that from 589 for the sun or from the lunar circuit for the moon to obtain the dusk fraction.

sentences.zh: 各以加夜半，如法為度。

translations.literal: Each use to add to midnight, by method as degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Add each fraction to the midnight longitude and reduce by the usual mansion rule.

sentences.zh: 推月蝕

translations.literal: Procedure: lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: lunar eclipse prediction.

sentences.zh: 置上元年，外所求，以會歲去之，其餘年以會率乘之，如會歲為積蝕，有餘加積一。

translations.literal: Set high origin years, outside the sought; remove by conjunction years; the remaining years multiply by conjunction rate; as conjunction years is accumulated eclipses; if there is remainder add accumulated one.
translations.idiomatic: From the epoch to the target year, take the remainder modulo 893, multiply by 1882, divide by 893—the quotient counts eclipse cycles, with any leftover incrementing the tally by one.

sentences.zh: 會月乘之，如會率為積月，不盡為月餘。

translations.literal: Conjunction months multiply it; as conjunction rate is accumulated months; not exhausted is month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply that count by 11045 and divide by 1882 for whole months; the residue is the fractional month part.

sentences.zh: 以章閏乘餘年，滿章歲為積閏，以減積月，餘以歲中去之，不盡，數起天正。

translations.literal: Multiply remaining years by metonic intercalation; what fills metonic years is accumulated intercalations; subtract from accumulated months; remainder remove by months in a year; not exhausted, count begins celestial standard.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply leftover years by 7, divide by 19 for leap months, subtract from the month total, then divide by 12; the remainder starts the count from the standard first month.

sentences.zh: 求次蝕，加五月，月餘千六百三十五，滿會率得一月，月以望。

translations.literal: Seek next eclipse: add five months, month remainder 1635; what fills conjunction rate obtains one month; month by full moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the next eclipse add five months plus remainder 1635; carry 1882 into another month; the eclipse falls at full moon.

sentences.zh: 推卦用事日

translations.literal: Procedure: hexagrams’ governing days.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: find the day each hexagram governs.

sentences.zh: 因冬至大餘，倍其小餘，坎用事日也。

translations.literal: Following winter solstice large remainder, double its small remainder; this is Kan’s governing day.
translations.idiomatic: Take the winter solstice stem-branch remainder and double the fractional part—that fixes the day when the Kan trigram takes charge.

sentences.zh: 加小餘千七十五，滿乾法從大餘，中孚用事日也。

translations.literal: Add small remainder 1075; what fills Qian divisor carries to large remainder; this is Zhongfu’s governing day.
translations.idiomatic: Add 1075 to the fraction, carry 1178 into the day count, and you have the Zhongfu governing day.

sentences.zh: 求次卦，各加大餘六，小餘百三。

translations.literal: Seek next hexagram: each add large remainder 6, small remainder 103.
translations.idiomatic: For each following hexagram add six to the large part and 103 to the small.

sentences.zh: 其四正各因共中日，而倍其小餘。

translations.literal: The four correct ones each follow their mid-day, and double their small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the four cardinal hexagrams, start from the solstice or equinox day and double the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 推五行用事

translations.literal: Procedure: five phases’ governing days.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: days when wood, fire, earth, metal, and water rule.

sentences.zh: 置冬至大小餘，加大餘二十七，小餘九百二十七，滿二千三百五十六從大餘，得土用事日也。

translations.literal: Set winter solstice large and small remainders; add large remainder 27, small remainder 927; what fills 2356 carries to large remainder; obtain earth governing day.
translations.idiomatic: From winter solstice add 27 days and 927 fractional parts, carrying 2356 into the day column, to reach the day earth governs.

sentences.zh: 加大餘十八，小餘六百一十八，得立春木用事日。

translations.literal: Add large remainder 18, small remainder 618; obtain Beginning of Spring wood governing day.
translations.idiomatic: Add 18 and 618 more to locate the day wood takes charge at Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: 加大餘七十三，小餘百一十六，復得土。

translations.literal: Add large remainder 73, small remainder 116; again obtain earth.
translations.idiomatic: Another 73 days and 116 parts brings earth back into authority.

sentences.zh: 又加土如得其火，金、水放此。

translations.literal: Again add as earth to obtain its fire; metal and water follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same step spacing for fire, then by analogy for metal and water.

sentences.zh: 推加時

translations.literal: Procedure: added double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: convert fractions into the twelve double-hours.

sentences.zh: 以十二乘小餘，滿其法得一辰，數從子起，算外，朔、弦、望以定小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply small remainder by twelve; what fills its divisor obtains one chen; count from zi beginning, outside the count; new moon, quarters, full moon use fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fractional day by 12 and divide by the day denominator to get the double-hour, counting from midnight zi; the remainder beyond the tally gives the exact moment for new, quarter, or full moon.

sentences.zh: 推漏刻

translations.literal: Procedure: clepsydra ke.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: convert day fractions into water-clock marks.

sentences.zh: 以百乘小餘，滿其法得一刻，不盡什之，求分，課所近節氣，起夜分盡；

translations.literal: Multiply small remainder by hundred; what fills its divisor obtains one ke; not exhausted divide by ten, seeking parts; test nearest qi, from night fraction exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Scale the fraction by 100, divide by the day law for whole ke, subdivide the tail by ten, and compare with the night run of the neighboring qi until the night watch runs out;

sentences.zh: 夜上水未盡，以所近言之。

translations.literal: Night upper water not yet exhausted; speak by what is nearest.
translations.idiomatic: if the clepsydra has not finished its night ascent, describe the time by the nearer boundary.

sentences.zh: 推有進退，進加退減所得也。

translations.literal: Procedure has advance and retreat; advance adds, retreat subtracts what is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Where the algorithm says advance, add the correction; where it says retreat, subtract it.

sentences.zh: 進退有差，起二分度後，率四度轉增少，少每半者，三而轉之，差滿三止，曆五度而減如初。

translations.literal: Advance and retreat have differences; starting after the two equinox degrees, generally every four degrees turn increases the small; small each half, thrice turn it; difference filling three stops; after five degrees of calendar subtract as at first.
translations.idiomatic: After the equinox points the correction steps change: roughly every four degrees the increment shrinks, halving each third step until the adjustment reaches three units, then after five degrees of travel the decrease resets like the start.

sentences.zh: 月行三道術

translations.literal: Method of the moon’s three paths.
translations.idiomatic: Theory of the moon moving along three paths.

sentences.zh: 月行遲疾，周進有恆。

translations.literal: Moon moves slow and fast; cycle advance has constancy.
translations.idiomatic: The moon speeds and slows, yet its cyclic advance follows a fixed law.

sentences.zh: 會數從天地凡數，乘餘率自乘，如會數而一，為過周分。

translations.literal: Conjunction number follows heaven-earth total number; multiply remainder rate self-multiplied; as conjunction number and one; is over-cycle fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Take the universal factor, multiply the residual rate by itself, and divide by 47 to obtain the over-cycle fraction.

sentences.zh: 以從周天，月周除之，曆日數也。

translations.literal: By following full heaven, divide by lunar circuit; this is calendar day count.
translations.idiomatic: Add this to the celestial circle and divide by the lunar circuit constant to get the tabulated day index.

sentences.zh: 遲疾有衰，其變者勢也。

translations.literal: Slow and fast have decay; what changes is the tendency.
translations.idiomatic: The speed variation itself ebbs and flows—that gradient is what shifts.

sentences.zh: 以衰減加月行率，為日轉度分。

translations.literal: By decay decrease add lunar motion rate; is daily revolution degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the decay correction to the mean lunar rate to yield the day’s sidereal motion in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 衰左右相加，為損益率。

translations.literal: Decay left and right add together; is increase-decrease rate.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the left and right decay terms to form the increase-or-decrease rate.

sentences.zh: 益轉相益，損轉相損，盈縮積也。

translations.literal: Increase turn mutually increases, decrease turn mutually decreases; is surplus-shrinkage accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Successive increases compound the surplus; successive decreases compound the shrinkage—those running totals are the waxing and waning integrals.

sentences.zh: 半小周乘通法，如通數而一，以曆周減焉，為朔行分也。

translations.literal: Half small cycle multiply tong divisor; as tong number and one; subtract by calendar week; is new-moon motion fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Take half of 254, multiply by the tong divisor, divide by 31, subtract from the calendar circumference—this yields the lunation opening fraction.

sentences.zh: 日轉度分列衰損益率盈縮積月行分一日十四度十分一退減益二十二盈初二百七十六二日十四度九分二退減益二十一盈二十二二百七十五三日十四度七分三退減益十九盈四十三二百七十三四日十四度四分四退減益十六盈六十二二百七十五日十四度四退減益十二盈七十八二百六十六六日十三度十五分四退減益八盈九十二百六十二七日十三度十一分四退減益四盈九十八二百五十八八日十三度七分四退減損盈百二二百五十四九日十三度三分四退加損四盈百二二百五十十日十二度十八分三退加損八盈九十八二百四十六十一日十二度十五分四退加損十一盈九十二百四十三十二日十二度十一分三退加損十五盈七十九二百三十九十三日十二度八分二退加損十八盈六十四二百三十六十四日十二度六分一退加損二十盈四十六二百三十四十五日十二度五分一進減損二十一盈二十六二百三十三十六日十二度六分二進減損二十損不足反減五為益，盈有五謂益

translations.literal: Column headings: daily revolution degrees and parts, listed decay, increase-decrease rate, surplus-shrinkage accumulation, lunar motion fraction; then tabulated rows for days 1–15 giving for each day the solar motion, retreat/decrease, increase or decrease, surplus value, and motion fraction, ending with the rule that when shrinkage is insufficient subtract five in reverse to obtain increase, and surplus five means increase.
translations.idiomatic: Tabulated ephemeris (first half-month): each line states the moon’s daily travel, the retreat-or-decrease flag, the additive correction, the running surplus tally (starting at 276), and the motion remainder; from day 8 the corrections switch from surplus to shrinkage, and the note explains how to flip a failed decrease into an increase once surplus hits five.

sentences.zh: 而損縮初二十，故不足。

translations.literal: Yet shrinkage’s beginning twenty, therefore insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Because the shrinkage column opens at twenty, early steps can fall short.

sentences.zh: 盈五縮初二百三十四十七日十二度八分三進減益十八縮十五二百三十六十八日十二度十一分四進減益十五縮二十三二百三十九十九日十二度十五分三進減益十一縮四十八二百四十三二十日十二度十八分四進減益八縮五十九二百四十六二十一日十三度三分四進減益四縮六十七二百五十二十二日十三度七分四進加損縮七十一二百五十四二十三日十三度十一分四進加損四縮七十一二百五十八二十四日十三度十五分四進加損八縮六十七二百六十二二十五日十四度四進加損十二縮五十九二百六十六二十六日十四度四分三進加損十六縮四十七二百七十二十七日十四度七分三曆初進加損十九縮三十一二百七十三

translations.literal: Surplus five shrinkage beginning 234; day 17 twelve degrees eight parts three advance decrease increase eighteen shrink fifteen 236; day 18 twelve degrees eleven parts four advance decrease increase fifteen shrink twenty-three 239; day 19 twelve degrees fifteen parts three advance decrease increase eleven shrink forty-eight 243; day 20 twelve degrees eighteen parts four advance decrease increase eight shrink fifty-nine 246; day 21 thirteen degrees three parts four advance decrease increase four shrink sixty-seven 250; day 22 thirteen degrees seven parts four advance add decrease shrink seventy-one 254; day 23 thirteen degrees eleven parts four advance add decrease four shrink seventy-one 258; day 24 thirteen degrees fifteen parts four advance add decrease eight shrink sixty-seven 262; day 25 fourteen degrees four advance add decrease twelve shrink fifty-nine 266; day 26 fourteen degrees four parts three advance add decrease sixteen shrink forty-seven 270; day 27 fourteen degrees seven parts three calendar beginning advance add decrease nineteen shrink thirty-one 273.
translations.idiomatic: Continuation of the lunar ephemeris from day 17 through day 27: surplus has dropped to five while shrinkage begins at 234, then each row advances the moon’s speed, adjusts the correction, and updates the shrinkage balance until the cycle nears its end at day 27.

sentences.zh: 三大周日周日十四度九分少進加損二十一縮十二二百七十五

translations.literal: Three great week day, week day fourteen degrees nine parts shao advance add decrease twenty-one shrink twelve 275.
translations.idiomatic: Final row of the third anomalistic week: fourteen degrees nine parts (slightly less), advance correction adding a loss of twenty-one, shrinkage twelve, balance 275.

sentences.zh: 周日分，三千三百三。

translations.literal: Week day fraction, 3303.
translations.idiomatic: Daily remainder numerator: 3303.

sentences.zh: 周虛，二千六百六十六。

translations.literal: Week void, 2666.
translations.idiomatic: Complement to complete the week denominator: 2666.

sentences.zh: 周日法，五千九百六十九。

translations.literal: Week day divisor, 5969.
translations.idiomatic: Week-day denominator: 5969.

sentences.zh: 通周，十八萬五千三十九。

translations.literal: Tong week, 185039.
translations.idiomatic: Full-cycle common numerator: 185,039.

sentences.zh: 曆周，十六萬四千四百六十六。

translations.literal: Calendar week, 164466.
translations.idiomatic: Anomalistic circumference constant: 164,466.

sentences.zh: 少大法，一千一百一。

translations.literal: Shao great divisor, 1111.
translations.idiomatic: Minor-difference master divisor: 1111.

sentences.zh: 朔行大分，萬一千八百一。

translations.literal: New-moon motion large fraction, 11801.
translations.idiomatic: Lunation opening major fraction: 11,801.

sentences.zh: 小分，二十五。

translations.literal: Small fraction, 25.
translations.idiomatic: Minor fraction: 25.

sentences.zh: 周半，一百二十七。

translations.literal: Week half, 127.
translations.idiomatic: Half-week index: 127.

sentences.zh: 推合朔入曆

translations.literal: Procedure: conjunction entering the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: place the syzygy inside the anomalistic month.

sentences.zh: 以上元積月乘朔行大小分，小分滿通數三十一從大分，大分滿曆周去之，余滿周法得一日，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: By high origin accumulated months multiply new-moon motion large and small fractions; small fraction filling tong number 31 carries to large fraction; large fraction filling calendar week remove it; remainder filling week divisor obtains one day; not exhausted is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply epoch months by the lunation fraction, carry 31 from the small into the large part, reduce modulo the anomalistic circumference, then divide by the week divisor for whole days and keep the tail as the day remainder.

sentences.zh: 日餘命算外，所求合朔入曆也。

translations.literal: Day remainder assign outside the count; this is the sought conjunction entering calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Count beyond the day remainder and you have the syzygy’s position within the tabulated month.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加一日，日餘五千八百三十二，小分二十五。

translations.literal: Seek next month, add one day, day remainder 5832, small fraction 25.
translations.idiomatic: For the following lunation add one day plus remainder 5832 and minor part 25.

sentences.zh: 求弦望，各加七日，日餘二千二百八十三，小分二十九半，分各如法成日，日滿二十七日去之。

translations.literal: Seek quarters and full moons, each add seven days, day remainder 2283, small fraction twenty-nine and a half; parts each by method complete days; days filling 27 remove them.
translations.idiomatic: For quarters and full moons add seven days, remainder 2283, and fraction 29½, carrying by the usual rules; drop multiples of 27 from the day count.

sentences.zh: 余如周分。

translations.literal: Remainder like week fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the remainder against the week fractional part.

sentences.zh: 不足除，減一日，加周虛。

translations.literal: Insufficient to divide, subtract one day, add week void.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction borrows, drop one day and add the week void constant.

sentences.zh: 求弦望定大小餘

translations.literal: Procedure: fixed large and small remainders for quarters and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: true fractional instants of quarters and full moons.

sentences.zh: 置所入曆盈縮積，以通周乘之為實。

translations.literal: Set entered calendar surplus-shrinkage accumulation; multiply by tong week as dividend.
translations.idiomatic: Take the tabulated surplus or shrinkage integral for the current day and multiply by 185,039 to form the dividend.

sentences.zh: 令通數乘日餘分，以乘損益率，以損益實，為加時盈縮也。

translations.literal: Order tong number multiply day remainder fraction; multiply by increase-decrease rate; by increase-decrease dividend; is added-hour surplus-shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the day remainder by 31, then by the increase-decrease rate, and apply that to the dividend to get the double-hour correction for surplus or shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 章歲減月行分，乘周半為差法，以除之，所得盈減縮加大小餘，如日法盈不足，朔加時在前後日。

translations.literal: Metonic years subtract lunar motion fraction; multiply week half as difference divisor; divide by it; what is obtained surplus subtract shrink add large and small remainders; like day law surplus insufficiency; new moon added hour on before-after day.
translations.idiomatic: Form the difference divisor from (19 minus the lunar rate) times 127, divide the correction by it, then subtract or add to the day fractions per surplus or shrinkage; if the day fraction overflows, roll the syzygy to the adjacent day.

sentences.zh: 弦望進退大餘，為定小餘。

translations.literal: Quarter and full moon advance-retreat large remainder; is fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The adjusted large remainder for quarters and full moons yields the definitive fractional day.

sentences.zh: 求朔弦望加時定度

translations.literal: Procedure: fixed degrees at syzygy and quarter phases.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: true longitudes at new moon, quarters, and full moon.

sentences.zh: 以章歲乘加時盈縮，差法除之，所得滿會數為盈縮大小分，以盈減縮加本日月所在，盈不足，以紀法進退度，為日月所在定度分。

translations.literal: Multiply metonic years by added-hour surplus-shrinkage; difference divisor divides it; what fills conjunction number is surplus-shrinkage large small fractions; by surplus subtract shrink add original sun moon place; surplus insufficiency; by era divisor advance-retreat degrees; is sun moon place fixed degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the double-hour surplus by 19, divide by the difference divisor, split the result into major and minor parts modulo 47, apply surplus-minus or shrinkage-plus to the base solar and lunar longitudes, borrowing 589 when needed—the outcome is the corrected degree and fraction.

sentences.zh: 推月行夜半入曆

translations.literal: Procedure: moon at midnight entering calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: place midnight within the anomalistic table.

sentences.zh: 以周半乘朔小餘，如通數而一，以減入曆日餘。

translations.literal: Multiply week half by new-moon small remainder; as tong number and one; subtract from entering-calendar day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the lunation fraction by 127, divide by 31, and subtract from the anomalistic day remainder.

sentences.zh: 余不足，加周法而減焉，卻一日。

translations.literal: Remainder insufficient, add week divisor and subtract therefrom; retreat one day.
translations.idiomatic: If the subtraction underflows, add the week divisor and back up one day.

sentences.zh: 卻得周日加其分，即得夜半入曆。

translations.literal: Retreat obtain week day add its parts; then obtain midnight entering calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After the retreat, add the weekly fractional part to reach midnight’s slot in the ephemeris.

sentences.zh: 求次日，轉一日，因日餘到二十七日，日余滿周日分去之，不直周日也。

translations.literal: Seek next day, turn one day; because day remainder reaches 27 days, day remainder filling week day fraction remove it; not hitting straight week day.
translations.idiomatic: Advance one tabulated day; when the remainder crosses 27 days, strip multiples of the week fraction unless you land exactly on a week boundary.

sentences.zh: 其不滿直之，加周虛于余，餘皆次日入曆日餘也。

translations.literal: Those not filling straight it; add week void to remainder; remainders all are next day entering-calendar day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not hit the boundary cleanly, add the week void to the residue—everything else becomes the next day’s anomalistic remainder.

sentences.zh: 求月夜半定度

translations.literal: Procedure: moon’s midnight fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: true lunar longitude at midnight.

sentences.zh: 以夜半入曆日餘，乘損益率，如周法得一，不盡為餘，以損益縮積，餘無所損，破全為法損之，為夜半盈縮也。

translations.literal: By midnight entering-calendar day remainder, multiply increase-decrease rate; as week divisor obtains one; not exhausted is remainder; by increase-decrease shrinkage accumulation; remainder nothing to decrease; break whole for divisor decrease it; is midnight surplus-shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the midnight remainder by the rate, divide by the week divisor, fold it into the shrinkage integral—if nothing cancels, borrow a unit and subtract—to get midnight’s surplus or shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 滿章歲為度，不盡為分。

translations.literal: Filling metonic years is degrees; not exhausted is parts.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 19 for whole degrees; the tail is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 通數乘分及余，余如周法從分，分滿紀法從度，以盈加縮減本夜半度及餘，為定度。

translations.literal: Tong number multiply parts and remainder; remainder like week divisor follows parts; parts filling era divisor follow degrees; by surplus add shrinkage subtract original midnight degree and remainder; is fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply fractions by 31, carry into parts per the week rule, carry 589 into degrees, then add surplus or subtract shrinkage from the midnight longitude for the definitive position.

sentences.zh: 求變衰法

translations.literal: Procedure: change-decay method.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: interpolate the decay correction.

sentences.zh: 以入曆日餘乘列衰，如周法得一，不盡為余，即穀知其日變衰也。

translations.literal: By entering-calendar day remainder multiply listed decay; as week divisor obtains one; not exhausted is remainder; then one knows that day’s change-decay.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the anomalistic remainder by the tabulated decay and divide by the week divisor; the quotient is how far the decay shifts on that day, reading the doubtful word in the text as meaning each successive step.

sentences.zh: 求次曆

translations.literal: Procedure: next calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: advance to the next anomalistic cycle.

sentences.zh: 以周虛乘列衰，如周法為常數，曆竟，輒以加變衰，滿列衰去之，轉為次曆變衰也。

translations.literal: Multiply week void by listed decay; as week divisor is constant; calendar finished, then add change-decay; filling listed decay remove it; turn into next calendar change-decay.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the void 2666 by the listed decay and divide by the week divisor for a constant increment; at cycle end add it to the change-decay modulo the table to seed the next lunation.

sentences.zh: 求次日夜半定度

translations.literal: Procedure: next day midnight fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: true midnight longitude on the following day.

sentences.zh: 以變衰進加退減曆日轉分，分盈不足，章歲出入度也。

translations.literal: By change-decay advance add retreat subtract calendar day revolution parts; parts surplus insufficiency; metonic years exit-enter degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the decay as advance-plus or retreat-minus to the daily motion fraction, carrying 19 into degrees when the fraction overflows or underflows.

sentences.zh: 通數乘分及餘，而日轉加夜定度，為次日也。

translations.literal: Tong number multiply parts and remainder; and day revolution add night fixed degree; is next day.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the fractional parts by 31, add the day’s motion to tonight’s fixed longitude, and you have tomorrow’s position.

sentences.zh: 竟曆不直周日，減餘三十八，乃以通數乘之，直周日者加餘八百三十七，又以少大分八百九十九，加次曆變衰，轉求如前。

translations.literal: Calendar end not hitting straight week day, subtract remainder thirty-eight; then multiply by tong number; hitting straight week day add remainder 837; also with shao large fraction 899, add next calendar change-decay; turn seek as before.
translations.idiomatic: If the cycle ends off the week boundary, subtract 38 from the remainder and scale by 31; if it lands on the boundary, add 837, then add 899 to the minor fraction and fold in the next cycle’s change-decay, repeating the same steps.

sentences.zh: 求次日夜半盈縮

translations.literal: Procedure: next day midnight surplus-shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: surplus or shrinkage at the next midnight.

sentences.zh: 以變衰減加損益率，為變損益率，而以轉損益夜半盈縮。

translations.literal: By change-decay decrease add increase-decrease rate; is changed increase-decrease rate; and by revolution increase-decrease midnight surplus-shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: Combine the decay with the base increase-decrease rate to form the adjusted rate, then let the daily revolution update midnight’s surplus or shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 曆竟損不足，反減為入次曆，減加餘如上數。

translations.literal: Calendar end decrease insufficient; reverse subtract as entering next calendar; subtract add remainder as above numbers.
translations.idiomatic: If the cycle closes with a failed decrease, invert the subtraction to enter the next ephemeris, adjusting remainders as in the rules above.

sentences.zh: 求昏明月度

translations.literal: Procedure: dusk and bright moon degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: lunar longitude at dusk and dawn.

sentences.zh: 以曆月行分乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一為明分。

translations.literal: Multiply calendar lunar motion fraction by nearest qi night clepsydra; two hundred and one for bright fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the tabulated lunar rate by the neighboring qi’s night water-clock reading and divide by 200 for the bright fraction.

sentences.zh: 以減月行分為昏分。

translations.literal: Subtract from lunar motion fraction for dusk fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that from the lunar rate to obtain the dusk fraction.

sentences.zh: 求月行遲疾

translations.idiomatic: Procedure: lunar anomaly in speed.

sentences.zh: 月經四表，出入三道，交錯分天，以月率除之，為曆之日。

translations.literal: Moon passes four markers, exits and enters three paths, interweaving dividing heaven; divide by monthly rate; is calendar days.
translations.idiomatic: As the moon crosses the four limits and weaves among three paths, partition the sky and divide by the monthly modulus to index the ephemeris day.

sentences.zh: 周天乘朔望合，如會月而一，朔合分也。

translations.literal: Full heaven multiply new-full conjunction; as conjunction month and one; new conjunction fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the celestial circumference by the syzygy conjunction and divide by 11045 for the conjunction fraction.

sentences.zh: 通數乘合數，餘如會數而一，退分也。

translations.literal: Tong number multiply conjunction number; remainder as conjunction number and one; retreat fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the conjunction count by 31 and reduce modulo 47 to obtain the retreat fraction.

sentences.zh: 以從月周，為日進分。

translations.literal: By following lunar circuit; is daily advance fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Add this to the lunar circuit to get the daily forward fraction.

sentences.zh: 會數而一，為差率也。

translations.literal: Conjunction number and one; is difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 47 to form the differential rate.

sentences.zh: 推朔入陰陽曆

translations.literal: Procedure: new moon entering yin-yang calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: place the new moon inside the solar-lunar latitude ephemeris.

sentences.zh: 以會月去上元積月，餘以朔合分及微分各乘之，微分滿其法從合分，合分滿周天去之，其餘不滿曆周者，為入陽曆；

translations.literal: By conjunction month remove high origin accumulated months; remainder multiply by new-moon conjunction fraction and micro-fraction each; micro-fraction filling its law carries to conjunction fraction; conjunction fraction filling full heaven remove it; the remainder not filling calendar week is entering yang calendar;
translations.idiomatic: Reduce epoch months modulo 11,045, scale by 18,328 and 914 with carries, reduce modulo the sky circle; a remainder under 107,565 means the moon is in the yang (north) column;

sentences.zh: 滿去之，餘為入陰曆。

translations.literal: Filling remove it; remainder is entering yin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: if it exceeds that, strip the cycle and the residue places the moon in the yin (south) column.

sentences.zh: 餘皆如月周得一日，算外，所求月合朔入曆，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: Remainder all like lunar circuit obtains one day, outside the count; sought month conjunction entering calendar; not exhausted is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the residue by the lunar circuit for whole days beyond the tally; what remains is the fractional day inside the table.

sentences.zh: 求次月

translations.literal: Seek next month.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: advance one lunation.

sentences.zh: 加二日，日餘二千五百八十，微分九百一十四，如法成日，滿十三去之，除餘如分日。

translations.literal: Add two days, day remainder 2580, micro-fraction 914, by method complete days, filling thirteen remove it, remove remainder like divide-day.
translations.idiomatic: Add two days plus remainder 2580 and micro-part 914, normalize, drop multiples of thirteen, and reconcile with the split-day rule.

sentences.zh: 陰陽曆竟互入端，入曆在前限餘前，後限餘後者月行中道也。

translations.literal: Yin-yang calendar end mutually enter end; entering calendar before front limit remainder front, after rear limit remainder rear means moon moves middle path.
translations.idiomatic: When the solar-lunar cycle flips, if the index falls before the front limit or after the rear limit, the moon is taken to ride the ecliptic mean.

sentences.zh: 求朔望定數

translations.literal: Seek new-full fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Procedure: true syzygy correction.

sentences.zh: 各置入遲疾曆盈縮大小分，會數乘小分為微分，盈減縮加陰陽日余，日餘盈不足，進退日而定。

translations.literal: Each set entered slow-fast calendar surplus-shrinkage large small parts; conjunction number multiply small part as micro-fraction; surplus subtract shrinkage add yin-yang day remainder; day remainder surplus insufficiency; advance retreat day and fix.
translations.idiomatic: Take the fast–slow surplus or deficit, turn the small part into micro-fractions with factor 47, add or subtract from the solar-lunar day fraction, and roll the day forward or back if it overflows.

sentences.zh: 以定日餘乘損益率，如月周得一，以損益兼數，為加時定數。

translations.literal: By fixed day remainder multiply increase-decrease rate; as lunar circuit obtains one; by increase-decrease combined number; is added-hour fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the corrected day fraction by the rate, divide by the lunar circuit, and apply the paired adjustment for the true syzygy instant.

sentences.zh: 推夜半入曆
